title: What's happening?
subtitle: Pick the closest match — we'll walk it through.

branches.label: Device doesn't connect (the computer doesn't see it)

node.title: Is the LED on when you plug the device into USB?
node.subtitle: Playtron and TouchMe do not light an LED when plugged in — a dark device is normal, so answer "Yes" for them. Scales, Biotron, and Orbita do have a status LED.

yes.title: Does the device show up in your operating system's MIDI list?
yes.subtitle: Mac: Audio MIDI Setup. Windows: Device Manager → Sound, video, game controllers.

yes.title: Most likely a browser problem.
fix: Open synth.playtronica.com in Chrome or Brave. Safari and Firefox don't speak MIDI.
Connect the device first, then open the browser tab. The page only scans for MIDI devices when it loads.
If you accidentally clicked Block on the MIDI permission popup, go to the browser's Site Settings → MIDI → set synth.playtronica.com to Allow.
yes.stuck: Send a short video showing: the device, your browser address bar, and the MIDI permission popup if it appears.

no.title: Likely a cable or port issue.
fix: Try a different USB cable (data cable, not a charge-only one).
Plug directly into the computer, not through a hub.
On Mac, open System Settings → Privacy & Security → check if any prompt is asking permission for the device.
no.stuck: Send the cable model + the port you're using + a screenshot of your OS's MIDI list (Mac: Audio MIDI Setup; Windows: Device Manager).

no.title: USB power isn't reaching the device.
fix: Try a different USB cable.
Plug into a different USB port — ideally directly on the computer, not a hub.
If you're on a thin laptop with USB-C only, make sure your adapter is a data adapter, not a charge-only one. Many cheap dongles are charge-only.
no.stuck: Send a photo of the device with the cable plugged in and the model of cable you're using.

node.title: Are you in Chrome or Brave?
node.subtitle: About 40% of 'no sound' cases resolve at this step.

yes.title: Did you click Allow on the MIDI permission popup?

node.title: Are you grounded — bare skin on the pointed corner of the device?

yes.title: Does the LED blink when you touch a clipped object?
Device works — the synth software is the problem.
fix: Try a different synth at synth.playtronica.com (Dots Piano is a reliable starting point).
Refresh the synth tab — sometimes the synth loses the MIDI connection after a few minutes.
If you're using a DAW, make sure a track is armed to receive MIDI and the volume isn't muted.

no.title: Likely a poor connection at the object end.
fix: Wet the object slightly — a damp finger across the surface usually helps.
Move the alligator clip to a different spot on the object — more contact area = stronger signal.
Try a known-good object (a banana, a piece of citrus) to confirm the device works, then go back to your original setup.

no.title: Grounding is the most common 'no sound' cause on Playtron.
fix: Put your bare hand on the pointed corner of Playtron — that sharp corner is the ground. Bare skin, not over clothing.
Or clip a ground cable from the pointed corner to a metal radiator, sink, or your laptop's metal body.
Test again with a fresh object.

node.title: Did Biotron calibrate?
node.subtitle: After connecting, leave it alone for 30 seconds. You should see a green LED blink then settle into a slow pulse.

yes.title: Likely a plant or contact issue.
fix: Make sure each leaf-pad is on a different branch or leaf, at least 2 cm apart.
Water the plant. Dry plants give weak signals.
Check that the synth's MIDI input is set to Channel 1 (the plant). Channel 2 is the light sensor — separate notes.

no.title: Run calibration from scratch.
fix: Unplug and replug the device. Move away. Wait 30 seconds.
If still no calibration sound, update the firmware via settings.playtronica.com/#/biotron in Chrome.
If calibration still fails after a firmware update, run the Nuke recovery.

node.title: Are you holding both gold pads with bare skin?

yes.title: Likely a synth issue.
fix: Try a different synth — Dots Piano is reliable.
Confirm the synth shows TouchMe in its MIDI device list.
Test with a MIDI monitor (MorningStar online) to see if TouchMe is sending notes regardless of the synth.

no.title: TouchMe needs both ends gripped to complete the circuit.
fix: Hold it like a remote control — one hand on each conductive pad.
Bare skin, not through a sleeve.
If you're sharing with a friend, both of you grip one end and touch each other — that also completes the circuit.

yes.title: Orbita is sending notes — the receiver isn't hearing them.
fix: Orbita doesn't make sound on its own. You need a synth or DAW receiving its MIDI.
In your DAW, set Orbita as a MIDI input and arm a track to receive.
Make sure the receiving track has a sound on it (instrument plugin or sample).

no.title: Orbita isn't rotating — likely power.
fix: Try a different USB cable and port.
If the LED is on but the motor doesn't spin, run the firmware update.

no.title: MIDI permission is the issue.
fix: Open your browser's settings → Site Settings → MIDI.
Find synth.playtronica.com in the list.
Set it to Allow.
Reload the synth page. The permission popup may reappear — click Allow.

no.title: Switch to Chrome or Brave.
fix: Web MIDI is only supported in Chromium-based browsers — Chrome, Brave, Edge.
Open synth.playtronica.com in one of those.
Connect the device first, then open the browser tab.

branches.label: Strange behaviour — random notes, wrong note per pin, weird timing

node.title: Do notes fire even when you don't touch the plant?

yes.title: Channel 2 (light sensor) is being triggered.
fix: The light sensor on Channel 2 is picking up flicker from LED bulbs, fluorescent lights, or your monitor.
Cover the light sensor with your hand to confirm — if the random notes stop, the light sensor is the cause.
Disable Channel 2 in settings.playtronica.com/#/biotron, or set it to CC only.

no.title: Likely an outdated firmware behaviour.
fix: Update the firmware via settings.playtronica.com/#/biotron in Chrome.
After update, run a fresh calibration (leave the device alone for 30 seconds).

node.title: Does a specific pin send a wrong note?

yes.title: A custom mapping was pushed to the device.
fix: Open settings.playtronica.com/#/playtron in Chrome.
Pick a preset (e.g. Major C) and click Send.
Or, in Custom mode, manually re-map each pin.

no.title: Try a fresh ground and a fresh object.
fix: Re-ground yourself (bare skin on the pointed corner).
Replace your test object with a known-good one (a banana).
If only certain pins act up, the alligator clips on those pins may be making poor contact — try wiggling them or swapping clips.

node.title: First, run a firmware update.
fix: Open settings.playtronica.com for your device in Chrome.
Update firmware to the latest version.
If the behaviour persists, run the Nuke recovery — it resets the device to a known state.
If it still persists after a Nuke, the issue is hardware. Email us with a video.

branches.label: Physical damage — USB connector loose, pin corroded, board cracked

node.title: Send us a photo — we'll sort it.
fix: Take a clear photo of the damage in good light.
Email support@playtronica.com with subject 'Defective #[your order number]'.
Include: photo, brief description, and your order number if you have it.
For corrosion on Playtron pins specifically, see the Playtron FAQ — light corrosion is fixable at home.

branches.label: Something else — describe in an email

node.title: Email us with as much detail as you can.
fix: Send a 30–60 second video showing the device, your screen, and what's not working.
Include: which device, your OS and browser, what you've already tried.
Email support@playtronica.com with subject 'Issue — [one-line description]'.
We reply in 1–3 business days.
